task.title: Review the board for use by several people at once
task.description:
The board was built for one trusted person on their own machine. "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" puts several people on one board, some of whom the team chose not to give the code to. This story checks what that changes and fixes what it finds, before hosting is recommended to anyone.

It is a review first. The board already takes care here: task text is built into the page as text and never as markup, pages are served with a content security policy, attachments outside a short list of safe types are sent as downloads, and request bodies have size limits. Those were all written with one user in mind. The question for each is whether it still holds when the person who wrote the text and the person reading it are different people.

## What to check

- **One person's text in another person's browser.** Titles, descriptions, comments, labels, attachment names, and the names of statuses, priorities and keys. Nothing a signed-in person types may run as code, or act on the board, in someone else's browser.
- **One person's attachment in another person's browser.** Which file types open in the page and which download, and whether an opened one can reach the board or the reader's session.
- **Links.** Where a link in task text can take someone, and whether it can carry anything from the board with it.
- **Limits.** Request and upload sizes, how many attachments a task may hold, and how many requests one person may have in flight. One signed-in person should not be able to fill the server's disk or stall the board for everyone else.
- **What a signed-in person can reach that a client should not.** Everything the web API offers, including changing statuses, priorities and keys, deleting tasks, and anything that reveals the server's folder, its remote address or its credential. There are no roles, so the answer is not to hide things per person; it is to know the list and state it in the hosting guide.
- **Error messages.** Whether a failure shown in the browser includes paths, remote addresses or command output from the server.

## Out of scope

- Roles or per-person permissions. Everyone the proxy lets in can do everything the board offers.
- The proxy and how it signs people in. That belongs to whoever deploys it.
- Protection against other websites driving the board at its public address. "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" covers that.

## Done when

- Each item above has a written finding on this task: what was tried, against a running board, and what happened.
- Every finding that lets one signed-in person harm another, or the server, is fixed here or is its own task that "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" depends on.
- Each fix has a test that fails without it.
- A list of what any signed-in person can do and see is written down, ready for the hosting guide to include.
- The board on a person's own machine behaves as it does today.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body:
Review record, 2026-11-21. The full written findings are attached as board-review-findings.md (what was tried against a running board for each of the six items, what happened, and the result), and the list of what any signed-in person can do and see is attached as board-review-capabilities.md and is in docs/reference.md. Three independent adversarial reviews re-ran the evidence; the files were corrected after each.

Outcome by item:
1. One person's text in another's browser: no script runs from any field. Fixed in PR #209: typed text is drawn without direction overrides everywhere the board draws it (titles, labels, tab titles, tooltips, file names, links), so a name cannot be disguised.
2. Attachments: non-image files always download and images open sandboxed. Fixed in PR #209: disguised file names in rows, references, history, image alt text and the download header.
3. Links: carry no referrer, opener or session. Sound.
4. Limits: per-request and per-task ceilings hold; nothing bounded work in flight or disk. Task "Cap how much work the board does at once" (v0.6.3, PR #211) adds a server-wide cap. Task "Give each signed-in person a budget on a hosted board" is in the backlog for boards that admit people a team does not trust.
5. What anyone can reach: listed by route. Anyone could rewrite anyone's comment under the author's name. Task "Let only a comment's author edit it" (v0.6.3, PR #213), decided by Dylan.
6. Error messages: a credential in the remote's address reached the browser. Fixed in PR #209 for the user name and password in a remote's address. Failure answers still name the server's folder and the remote's address; "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" replaces them with a short sentence on a hosted board (noted on that task).

"Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" depends on both v0.6.3 tasks above.
